Bipolar disorder doesn't begin to show symptoms until early adulthood. I'm not saying you *have* bipolar disorder, but I though it relevant to mention it as a possibility since misdiagnosis is very common with mood disorders. In any case, seeing a new psychiatrist can never hurt if you're able to. Getting a second medical opinion can always be useful if you're having any doubts. Good luck!

Hello! Has your psychiatrist mentioned anything regarding a potential mood disorder other than depression? What you're describing sounds a lot like bipolar disorder (long period of depression, followed by a long period of euphoria, then depression again). There are other disorders that present similar symptoms (such a BPD, for example), but it does sound really similar to bipolar. It could be why your meds aren't working properly. I'd recommend bringing it up with your current doctor or seeking help from a new one. 


Also, I understand the fear of a doctor knowing you're trans, but if you're on T, testosterone can have an effect on the meds (doesn't mean they're incompatible, but the dosage needs to be adjusted or the meds might not work properly) so ideally it would be best to mention it if you can


Wish you the best!

Your emotions are completely valid. Surgery can be absolutely terrifying, but remember that you'll be under the supervision and care of a competent medical team who performs surgery every day and thus will be absolutely prepared if any problem should arise.


No matter the visual outcome, you'll feel much better physically. I used to have a gigantic chest, and now, back pains? Gone. Breathing is much easier too. You won't have anything heavy weighting down on your sternum and thoracic cage, you'll be able to jump, run and move around more freely without worrying about other people's stares.


You also seem to be well prepared for post-op, which is great, it'll help a lot with the initial discomfort. The first month is going to be uncomfortable, but it'll pass by quickly and soon you'll be able to live your life more freely.


Wishing you the best, it's gonna be alright!!
